verses.text: They crossed the lake and arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an impure spirit came from the tombs to meet him.
The man lived among the tombs, and no one could restrain him anymore, not even with a chain.
He’d often been bound with shackles and chains, but he tore the chains apart and broke the shackles. No one was strong enough to control him.
Night and day among the tombs and in the hills, he shouted and cut himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from far away, he ran up and fell on his knees before him.
He shouted, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Swear by God you won’t torture me!”
For Jesus had already said to him, “Come out of the man, impure spirit!”
Jesus asked him, “What’s your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because there are many of us.”
The spirits begged Jesus over and over not to send them out of the region.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby hillside.
The spirits begged him, “Send us into the pigs. Let us go into them.”
Jesus gave them permission. The impure spirits came out and went into the pigs. The herd—about two thousand—rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The men who had been tending the pigs ran off and reported it in the town and countryside. People came to see what had happened.
When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who’d been controlled by the legion sitting there, dressed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what happened to the man and to the pigs.
Then the people began begging Jesus to leave their region.
As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who’d been demon-possessed begged to go with him.
Jesus wouldn’t let him. Instead he said, “Go home to your family and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he’s shown you mercy.”
So the man went away and began telling people in the Ten Cities how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.
When Jesus crossed back by boat, a large crowd gathered around him beside the lake.
One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came over. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
and begged earnestly, “My little daughter is dying. Please come and lay your hands on her so she can be healed and live.”
Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around him.
A woman in the crowd had been bleeding for twelve years.
She’d suffered a lot under many doctors, spent all she had, and instead of getting better, she’d grown worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
She thought, “If I can just touch his clothes, I’ll be healed.”
Immediately her bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was healed from her suffering.
Right away Jesus realized power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said, “You see the crowd pressing in on you, and you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it.
The woman, trembling with fear because she knew what had happened to her, came and fell at his feet and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering.”
While Jesus was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s house and said, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the teacher anymore?”
Jesus heard what they said and told the synagogue leader, “Don’t be afraid. Just believe.”
He didn’t let anyone follow him except Peter, James, and James’ brother John.
When they arrived at the synagogue leader’s home, Jesus saw the commotion, people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went in and said, “Why all this noise and crying? The child isn’t dead; she’s sleeping.”
They laughed at him. But he sent everyone out, took the child’s father and mother and his companions, and went in where the child was.
He took the girl by the hand and said, “Talitha koum!”—which means, “Little girl, I’m telling you, get up!”
Immediately the girl stood up and began walking around. She was twelve years old. They were completely amazed.
Jesus strictly ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened, and told them to give her something to eat.
